title: Cue library and experimentation canvas for enterprise model-fit
creator: Priya Desai
description: Goal: Build a lightweight, reproducible "cue library" that maps observable enterprise usage signals to recommended priority for model onboarding and experiments. The cue library is a curated taxonomy of behavioral/operational indicators (e.g., average query length, multiline prompt prevalence, embedding throughput, RAG recall sensitivity, SLO tolerance) plus rules for scoring and grouping customers into model-fit cohorts. The deliverable is: (1) a documented cue catalog, (2) a prioritization heuristic + scoring script, and (3) an experimentation canvas (sample selection, metric definitions, rollout triggers) for 3 priority customers. This ticket focuses on product research and the hypothesis-driven experiment design; engineering work for telemetry and scoring integration will be tracked as follow-ups.
acceptance_criteria: Cue catalog published in Confluence with sources and example customer snippets
Scoring heuristic (python script) that consumes sample telemetry and outputs a model-fit score (repo + README)
Experimentation canvas completed for 3 enterprise cohorts (sampling plan, metrics, guardrails, rollback criteria)
Sign-off from two PM stakeholders and one engineering owner on feasibility and telemetry gaps
Pilot experiment scheduled with Solutions team for one pilot customer by due_date.
comments: 2025-02-18 Priya Desai: Kickoff — sketched initial cue buckets: request-profile (tokens, concurrency, avg seq), retrieval-dependence (RAG use, embed queries per session), safety-sensitivity (sensitive entity rates), SLA-tolerance (99th latency vs mean), cost-sensitivity (tokens per user), and personalization-degree. Added raw examples from 4 anonymized customers.

2025-02-21 Miguel Ortega: Engineering feasibility review — core telemetry exists for tokens and latency, but retrieval dependency and per-user personalization signals require small agent-side instrumentation. Logged ENG-80712 to add per-session embed counters and ENG-80713 for per-route sampling tags.

2025-02-25 Design review (Aisha Khan): UX note — experiments must surface simplest statement to sales/customer-success: 'Likelihood this customer benefits from model X' and provide top-3 cues. Will prototype a compact dashboard card. Linked design quick mock: https://drive.google.com/file/d/1design-mock

2025-02-28 Priya Desai: Trade-offs discussion — aggressive prioritization favors customers with high RAG-dependence and low SLA tolerance but that increases infra cost. Decision: initial scoring will weight recall-sensitivity 1.5x and SLA-tolerance 1.2x; document as parameterized weights in repo for later calibration.

2025-03-01 Solutions feedback (Daniel Wu): Suggested sampling: include one greenfield startup (high tokens, low personalization), one mid-enterprise SaaS (moderate tokens, high RAG), and one regulated-finance customer (low tokens, high safety-sensitivity). Added to experimentation canvas.

2025-03-03 Miguel Ortega: Blocker noted — access to customer-level RAG recall metrics requires privacy review. Filed security checkbox: security_review_required set to true on the follow-up engineering ticket ENG-80714. For this ticket, we will mock RAG recall using sampled queries.
